name: Botrytis (grey mould)
description: Fungal disease that thrives in damp, still air. Major BOP greenhouse problem May–Aug.
symptoms: Fuzzy grey mould on flowers, fruit, and stems; soft rotting tissue.
conditions: RH above 80 % and temperatures between 15 and 22 °C.
controls: Remove old leaves and rotting fruit

name: Powdery mildew
description: White powdery fungal growth on leaves, especially cucurbits and tomatoes.
symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces; yellowing; premature leaf drop.
conditions: Warm days, cool nights, moderate humidity, and poor airflow.

name: Tomato late blight
description: Devastating fungal-like disease that can wipe out a tomato crop in days.
symptoms: Brown, water-soaked patches on leaves and stems; white sporulation underneath; rapid collapse.
conditions: Aug–Oct wet spells with cool, humid weather.
controls: Keep foliage dry — water at the base
Preventive copper spray before wet spells
Remove and bin (don't compost) infected plants

name: Damping off
description: Seedling collapse caused by soil-borne fungi (Pythium, Rhizoctonia).
symptoms: Seedlings topple at soil line; stems pinched and dark; sudden death.
conditions: Cold, wet seed-raising mix and overcrowded trays.

name: Tomato spotted wilt virus (TSWV)
description: Viral disease vectored by thrips. No cure — focus on prevention.
symptoms: Bronzed, ringed spots on leaves; stunted growth; deformed fruit.
conditions: Where thrips are present and uncontrolled.

name: Citrus gall wasp
description: Tiny wasp whose larvae cause woody galls on citrus stems.
symptoms: Swollen green or woody galls on new citrus stems; weakened growth.
conditions: Citrus across northern NZ; emerges Sep–Nov.
controls: Prune out and bag galls Jun–Aug before wasp emerges

name: Blossom end rot
description: Disorder (not a disease) caused by erratic watering and calcium uptake issues.
symptoms: Sunken, dark, leathery patch on the blossom end of fruit.
conditions: Inconsistent watering; high transpiration; calcium-deficient soil.
controls: Water consistently — mulch to even soil moisture

name: Clubroot
description: Soil-borne pathogen that causes swollen, distorted brassica roots.
symptoms: Wilting plants despite damp soil; swollen, club-shaped roots; stunted growth.
conditions: Acidic, wet, poorly drained soils growing brassicas in succession.
controls: Rotate brassicas on a 4+ year cycle
